primary_secondary.note: Journal extension of the authors' ICSE-SEIP 2026 paper; RQ3 results summarized from it.

study_type.note: Multimodal field study with controlled (A/B) sessions and an uncontrolled everyday-work period.

research_method.claude: Mixed-methods multimodal field study: controlled sessions with A/B design plus uncontrolled real-work period; Likert/open questionnaires, annotated screen recordings, workday questionnaire; descriptive statistics, Kendall's tau, (G)LMMs, Mann-Whitney U, Cohen's d, qualitative content analysis
research_method.nlm: Mixed-methods 4-day field study combining controlled sessions with uncontrolled natural work periods; linear mixed-effects models, Cohen's d, Kendall's tau, qualitative content analysis; ~66 h screen recordings, 445 logged tasks
research_method.value: 4-day mixed-methods field study: two controlled sessions (Java tasks, A/B design with/without GitHub Copilot, NASA-TLX after each task) around three days of uncontrolled everyday work (workday questionnaires, 445 tasks); pre/post questionnaires, ~66 h annotated screen recordings; (generalized) linear mixed-effects models, Kendall's tau, Cohen's d, qualitative content analysis (Mayring & Fenzl)
research_method.note: Mann-Whitney U reported only by Claude; HumanEval-X task selection only by NotebookLM (both not contradicted). Physiological/keyboard data collected but not analysed.

evidence.quote: Over a period of four days, we observed 22 developers in how they use GenAI tools in controlled and uncontrolled settings.
Half of the participants did not use Copilot during the tasks of the first controlled session, whilst the other half did (Figure 1, A/B study design).
To predict task completion, duration, and perceived workload during the controlled sessions, (generalized) linear mixed-effects models were used.

The 445 working tasks documented by the participants in the workday questionnaire (Figure 1) were categorized into three general categories: development-heavy, collaboration-heavy and other activities.
The participant cohort consisted of twenty-two SAP employees from two firm sites in California, USA.
the Copilot evaluation questionnaire (based on the SPACE framework [14] and adapted to evaluate specifically Copilot) was filled in after the baseline tasks.
The developer experience (DevEx) framework highlights three main factors that impact DevEx: cognitive load, flow state, and feedback loop [33].
we examine the cognitive load aspect together with the feedback loop in this paper

the impact of Copilot on task efficiency (task duration), accuracy (task completion) and perceived workload during the controlled sessions of the study was analyzed in detail based on the screen recordings and the NASA-TLX scores.
interaction characteristics with Copilot (with or without Copilot use, number of in-code suggestions and number of chat prompts).
most participants reported being either satisfied (n=11) or very satisfied (n=5) (72.73%) with none expressing dissatisfaction.
According to the median (Md=4), participants agree that they turn more quickly to GenAI tools for feedback than to fellow team members.
